search.string: (Denmark OR Danish) AND ("register data" OR "registry data" OR "register-based" OR "administrative data" OR "administrative records" OR "population register" OR "Statistics Denmark" OR "full population" OR "employer-employee")

nodes.label: Academic self-efficacy
nodes.summary: Academic self-efficacy is how much a pupil believes he can cope with schoolwork.

nodes.label: Co-workers as the reference group
nodes.summary: Whether someone measures his income against his colleagues instead of against everyone.

nodes.label: Misperception of own income rank
nodes.summary: Whether people know where they really stand in the income distribution of the group they compare themselves with.

nodes.label: Overestimation of own income rank
nodes.summary: How much people flatter themselves about their position in the income ranking of their neighbours or colleagues.

nodes.label: Underestimation of others' incomes
nodes.summary: How much people underestimate what the others around them earn.

nodes.label: Information about re-employment wages of comparable workers
nodes.summary: This is how much a jobseeker is told about what comparable workers actually earn when they get re-employed.

nodes.label: Consumption
nodes.summary: How much is spent on goods and services, for a household or for the economy as a whole.

nodes.label: Marginal propensity to consume
nodes.summary: How much of an extra krone a household spends instead of saving it.

nodes.label: Visible consumption signalling income
nodes.summary: How far someone's spending puts his income on show to his neighbours.

nodes.label: Criminal capital
nodes.summary: Criminal capital is the know-how and contacts that make someone better at committing crime.

nodes.label: Criminal history
nodes.summary: Criminal history is how much past crime a person has been charged with or convicted of.

nodes.label: Drug offending
nodes.summary: Drug offending is being charged with a drug crime such as possession.

nodes.label: Distance of the prison placement from home
nodes.summary: How far from home the prison an inmate is held in is.

nodes.label: Transfer between custodial facilities
nodes.summary: Being moved from one prison or jail to another during a sentence.

nodes.label: Record of imprisonment
nodes.summary: Whether someone has been to prison.

nodes.label: Placement in a jail rather than a prison
nodes.summary: Whether someone is held in a local jail instead of a proper prison.

nodes.label: Placement in an open prison
nodes.summary: Whether an inmate is held in an open, low-security prison rather than a closed one.

nodes.label: Exposure to peers in other crime types
nodes.summary: Exposure to peers in other crime types is how many of a prisoner's fellow inmates specialize in crimes different from his own.

nodes.label: Exposure to peers in the same crime type
nodes.summary: Exposure to peers in the same crime type is how many of a prisoner's fellow inmates specialize in his own kind of crime.

nodes.label: Recidivism
nodes.summary: Recidivism is reoffending after a conviction or release from prison.

nodes.label: Length of the prison sentence
nodes.summary: How long the prison sentence is.

nodes.label: Academic summer camp with follow-up program
nodes.summary: Taking part in a summer school for struggling pupils plus a year of follow-up support.

nodes.label: Group mentoring in the follow-up program
nodes.summary: The part of the programme where students are mentored in small groups during the year after camp.

nodes.label: Enrolment in the academic upper-secondary track
nodes.summary: Whether a pupil goes on to the academic high-school track.

nodes.label: School achievement
nodes.summary: How well a child does on school tests.

nodes.label: Non-completion of the ninth-grade assessment
nodes.summary: Whether a pupil never finishes the ninth-grade exam.

nodes.label: Comparative advantage in language over math
nodes.summary: How far a student's language results run ahead of his math results.

nodes.label: Educational attainment
nodes.summary: Educational attainment is how much schooling a person ends up completing.

nodes.label: Dropping out of education
nodes.summary: Leaving a course of study before finishing it.

nodes.label: Inequality in educational outcomes
nodes.summary: How far apart people's educational outcomes are from one another.

nodes.label: Returns to genetic endowments in education
nodes.summary: How much a person's genetic predisposition for schooling actually shows up in the education he gets.

nodes.label: Human capital
nodes.summary: The skills and capacities a person has built up, broader than the schooling or test scores used to measure them.

nodes.label: Access to middle school
nodes.summary: This is how easily a child can get to a middle school in the place he grows up.

nodes.label: On-time school progression
nodes.summary: Whether a pupil moves through school on schedule rather than falling behind a year.

nodes.label: Access to preschool
nodes.summary: Access to preschool is whether a child can get a place in publicly provided early education.

nodes.label: Relative age within the school cohort
nodes.summary: Relative age is how old a child is compared with his classmates.

nodes.label: Subsidies for retraining
nodes.summary: A retraining subsidy is public money that pays for an adult to go back to school and learn a new trade.

nodes.label: School absence
nodes.summary: School absence is how many days of school a pupil misses.

nodes.label: Planned (legal) school absence
nodes.summary: This is the school a pupil misses on leave the school approved beforehand.

nodes.label: School absence due to illness
nodes.summary: This is the school a pupil misses because he is ill.

nodes.label: School connectedness
nodes.summary: School connectedness is how much a pupil feels he belongs at his school.

nodes.label: School quality
nodes.summary: How good the schools a child can attend are.

nodes.label: Completion of tertiary education
nodes.summary: Whether someone graduates from college.

nodes.label: Enrolment in higher education
nodes.summary: This is whether a person enrols in a college or university degree.

nodes.label: Enrolment in a field related to past experience
nodes.summary: This is whether the degree someone goes back to study builds on what he already knows and has done.

nodes.label: Publicly provided training capacity
nodes.summary: Training capacity is how many publicly funded study places a field is given to train new entrants.

nodes.label: Completion of upper secondary education
nodes.summary: Whether someone graduates from high school.

nodes.label: Enrolment in the vocational upper-secondary track
nodes.summary: This is whether a student goes on to a vocational programme after compulsory school.

nodes.label: Abortion
nodes.summary: Whether a pregnancy is terminated rather than carried to term.

nodes.label: Adoption rather than out-of-home care
nodes.summary: This is whether a child taken from his birth parents is adopted into a new family instead of being placed in care.

nodes.label: Birth order
nodes.summary: Whether a child is an older or a younger sibling.

nodes.label: Child-bearing age window
nodes.summary: The narrow band of years in which women can have children, and whether a woman is in it now.

nodes.label: Cohabitation
nodes.summary: Whether a person shares a household with a partner.

nodes.label: Divorce
nodes.summary: Whether a marriage breaks up.

nodes.label: Dependence on family members for support
nodes.summary: How much a person has to lean on relatives for the basics, with no claim of her own.

nodes.label: Assortative mating on education
nodes.summary: How strongly people pair up with partners whose education matches their own.

nodes.label: Family background
nodes.summary: Everything siblings share by being raised in the same family, treated as a single influence on how their lives turn out.

nodes.label: Quality of interactions within the family
nodes.summary: How well the people in a family get on and engage with one another at home.

nodes.label: Childbearing
nodes.summary: Having children -- the number of children a person has.

nodes.label: Having another child
nodes.summary: Adding a child to those a person already has -- the intensive margin of fertility.

nodes.label: Share of births to more-advantaged mothers
nodes.summary: This is who is having the children: how far births are concentrated among better-off women rather than worse-off ones.

nodes.label: Becoming a parent
nodes.summary: Going from no children to a first child -- the extensive margin of fertility.

nodes.label: Gender-specialized parenting
nodes.summary: How far parents split the raising of sons and daughters along gender lines.

nodes.label: Grandparents' division of labor
nodes.summary: How traditional the division of paid work was in a parent's own childhood home: how little the grandmother worked compared with the grandfather.

nodes.label: Maternal grandparents' division of labor
nodes.summary: How traditional the division of paid work was between the mother's own parents.

nodes.label: Paternal grandparents' division of labor
nodes.summary: How traditional the division of paid work was between the father's own parents.

nodes.label: Gendered division of household production
nodes.summary: This is how lopsidedly a couple divides housework and childcare between the woman and the man.

nodes.label: Care received from adult children
nodes.summary: How much hands-on help an older person gets from his grown-up children.

nodes.label: Intergenerational persistence of financial trouble
nodes.summary: How closely children's debt trouble tracks that of their parents.

nodes.label: Intergenerational persistence of income
nodes.summary: This is how closely how much someone earns tracks how much his parents earned.

nodes.label: Intergenerational persistence of wealth
nodes.summary: This is how closely someone's wealth tracks the wealth of his parents.

nodes.label: Intermarriage
nodes.summary: Intermarriage is being married to a spouse from a different national or ethnic origin group.

nodes.label: IVF treatment success
nodes.summary: Whether an IVF treatment results in a live birth.

nodes.label: Marriage
nodes.summary: Whether people marry.

nodes.label: Disadvantage in the local marriage market
nodes.summary: How little chance someone has of finding a spouse where she lives.

nodes.label: Parent-specific transmission
nodes.summary: This is how much a child's economic position comes from one parent in particular rather than from the family as a whole.

nodes.label: Parents' age at the child's birth
nodes.summary: This is how old a mother or father is at the birth of the child.

nodes.label: Parental compensating investment
nodes.summary: How much parents redirect their time and resources toward the child who needs them most.

nodes.label: Parental death
nodes.summary: The death of a person's parent.

nodes.label: Parental default
nodes.summary: Whether a person's parent defaulted on debt.

nodes.label: Parental health
nodes.summary: Parental health is how healthy a child's mother or father is.

nodes.label: Parental job loss
nodes.summary: A child's parent losing their job.

nodes.label: Parental job loss in adolescence
nodes.summary: A parent losing their job while the child was a teenager.

nodes.label: Parental job loss in early childhood
nodes.summary: A parent losing their job while the child was a preschooler.

nodes.label: Parents' preferences
nodes.summary: The tastes over risk and the timing of money that a person's parents hold.

nodes.label: Traditionalness of the chosen partner
nodes.summary: How traditional the gender roles of the partner a person chooses are.

nodes.label: Sibling's disability
nodes.summary: Growing up with a brother or sister who has a disability.

nodes.label: Sibling sex composition
nodes.summary: Whether the sibling a person grows up with is a brother rather than a sister.

nodes.label: Sibling similarity in earnings
nodes.summary: How closely siblings' earnings resemble one another, the standard measure of how much family origins matter for pay.

nodes.label: Sibling similarity in education
nodes.summary: How closely siblings' schooling resembles one another's, a measure of how much family origins matter for education.

nodes.label: Sibling similarity in unemployment
nodes.summary: How closely siblings resemble one another in spells of unemployment, a measure of how much family origins matter for joblessness.

nodes.label: Marriage to a spouse from abroad
nodes.summary: Marrying someone from another country and bringing them home.

nodes.label: Unpaid care work
nodes.summary: How much unpaid caring for family members a person has to do.

nodes.label: Innovation
nodes.summary: How much a firm invents and brings new products or processes into use.

nodes.label: Organizational capital
nodes.summary: The management practices and organizational know-how a firm has built up as an asset.

nodes.label: Firm production technology
nodes.summary: The way a firm's production is technically organized, which shapes how work and hours must fit together.

nodes.label: Firm productivity
nodes.summary: How productive a firm is.

nodes.label: Firm profits
nodes.summary: How much money a firm makes.

nodes.label: R&D capital
nodes.summary: The accumulated research and development know-how a firm owns and produces with.

nodes.label: Share of R&D workers
nodes.summary: How big a part of the staff works in research and development.

nodes.label: Robot adoption
nodes.summary: Robot adoption is how far a firm has taken up industrial robots in its production.

nodes.label: Firm size
nodes.summary: How many people work at the firm.

nodes.label: Employer wage premium
nodes.summary: The pay bonus a worker gets simply from which firm employs him.

nodes.label: Alcohol consumption
nodes.summary: How much a person drinks, including bouts of heavy drinking.

nodes.label: Alcohol poisoning
nodes.summary: Whether a person ends up in medical care for acute alcohol poisoning.

nodes.label: Birth weight
nodes.summary: How much a baby weighs when it is born.

nodes.label: Regulation of dental care provision
nodes.summary: Regulation of dental care is the set of rules telling dentists how often to recall patients and what services are paid for.

nodes.label: Disability
nodes.summary: Disability is being unable to work because of health, as registered through disability pension award.

nodes.label: General health
nodes.summary: General health is how healthy a person is overall.

nodes.label: Health care use
nodes.summary: How much medical care and medication a person takes up.

nodes.label: Annual control visits for chronic disease
nodes.summary: How often chronic patients get their yearly check-up.

nodes.label: Use of prescribed contraception
nodes.summary: How much prescribed birth control a person uses.

nodes.label: Frequency of dental recalls
nodes.summary: Dental recall frequency is how often patients are called back for a dental check-up.

nodes.label: Diagnostic services
nodes.summary: Diagnostic services are the examinations and imaging part of the care delivered.

nodes.label: Medical treatment in early life
nodes.summary: How much medical treatment a child receives in his earliest years.

nodes.label: Use of public eldercare services
nodes.summary: How much public eldercare help an older person actually uses.

nodes.label: Emergency department use
nodes.summary: This is how often a person turns up at a hospital emergency department for acute care.

nodes.label: Hospital expenditure
nodes.summary: How much is spent on hospital treatment.

nodes.label: Prescriptions for opioids
nodes.summary: Whether a person fills prescriptions for opioid painkillers.

nodes.label: Preventive dental care
nodes.summary: Preventive dental care is the share of dental treatment that is prophylaxis and cleaning rather than repair.

nodes.label: Preventive home visits
nodes.summary: How often a doctor makes preventive visits to patients at home.

nodes.label: Use of psychiatric care
nodes.summary: How often someone is treated at a psychiatric clinic.

nodes.label: Use of psychological assistance
nodes.summary: How often a person visits a psychologist.

nodes.label: Prescriptions for mental health conditions
nodes.summary: Whether a person fills prescriptions for mental health medication.

nodes.label: Vaccine take-up
nodes.summary: Whether someone gets vaccinated when a vaccine is available to them.

nodes.label: Inequality in health care take-up
nodes.summary: How far apart high- and low-status groups are in how much care and vaccination they take up.

nodes.label: Severe health shock
nodes.summary: A sudden severe health event striking a household member -- in these data a heart attack or a stroke.

nodes.label: Fatal health shock
nodes.summary: A health event that killed the household member -- for the survivor, the death of a spouse.

nodes.label: Nonfatal health shock
nodes.summary: A severe health event the household member survived.

nodes.label: Hospital readmission
nodes.summary: Hospital readmission is a patient coming back into hospital soon after being discharged.

nodes.label: Infectious disease
nodes.summary: This is how much infectious illness a person gets, read from hospital admissions for infections.

nodes.label: Physical injury
nodes.summary: A physical injury is bodily harm a person suffers in an accident.

nodes.label: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis
nodes.summary: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis is a chronic joint disease that begins in childhood.

nodes.label: Mental health
nodes.summary: A person's psychological well-being.

nodes.label: Bipolar disorder
nodes.summary: Bipolar disorder is a diagnosed mood disorder with manic and depressive episodes.

nodes.label: Depression
nodes.summary: Depression is a diagnosed depressive illness, one of the mental disorders whose presence marks worse mental health.

nodes.label: Schizophrenia
nodes.summary: Schizophrenia is a diagnosed psychotic disorder.

nodes.label: Mortality
nodes.summary: Mortality is whether people die within a given period.

nodes.label: Inequality in survival across socioeconomic groups
nodes.summary: This is how far apart the survival chances of low- and high-status groups are.

nodes.label: Exposure to the COVID-19 pandemic
nodes.summary: This is whether someone lived through the COVID-19 pandemic and its closures at the point in life being studied.

nodes.label: Quality of prescribing
nodes.summary: How well a doctor's prescriptions follow good practice.

nodes.label: Preterm birth
nodes.summary: Preterm birth is being born too early, before the pregnancy has run its full term.

nodes.label: Providers' financial motivation
nodes.summary: How much a doctor is driven by what a treatment pays.

nodes.label: Non-paternalistic altruism toward patients
nodes.summary: How far a doctor gives patients what they ask for rather than what is good for them.

nodes.label: Proximity to death
nodes.summary: How close someone is to dying.

nodes.label: Respiratory illness
nodes.summary: How much respiratory disease a person suffers.

nodes.label: Chronic respiratory illness
nodes.summary: Whether a person has lasting lung disease.

nodes.label: Early-life respiratory disease
nodes.summary: Whether a child caught a serious respiratory illness as an infant.

nodes.label: Risky sexual behaviour
nodes.summary: How much a person engages in sex that risks pregnancy or infection.

nodes.label: Sexually transmitted infection
nodes.summary: Whether a person is diagnosed with a sexually transmitted infection such as chlamydia.

nodes.label: Access to treatment
nodes.summary: Access to treatment is how easily care for a condition can be obtained.

nodes.label: Type 1 diabetes
nodes.summary: Whether a person develops type 1 diabetes, a lifelong insulin-dependent illness that in these data strikes during childhood.

nodes.label: Unmet care needs
nodes.summary: How much of the help someone needs in daily life nobody is providing.

nodes.label: Vaccination program
nodes.summary: A public programme offering a free vaccine to a given group of people.

nodes.label: Order of vaccines in the immunization schedule
nodes.summary: This is the order a child's shots come in — whether the live MMR vaccine follows the third DTaP dose rather than preceding it.

nodes.label: Work capacity
nodes.summary: How far someone's health lets them keep working.

nodes.label: House prices
nodes.summary: How expensive homes are in a local housing market.

nodes.label: Listing price
nodes.summary: The price a seller asks for when listing a home for sale.

nodes.label: Nominal gain on the home relative to its purchase price
nodes.summary: How much a home is worth now compared with what the owner paid for it in kroner.

nodes.label: Dependence on public benefits
nodes.summary: This is how much of a person's income comes from public benefits rather than from work.

nodes.label: Capital income
nodes.summary: Income from assets -- interest, dividends and other returns to capital -- as reported for tax.

nodes.label: Household disposable income
nodes.summary: Total income of the household after taxes and public transfers.

nodes.label: Labor income
nodes.summary: The money a person earns from work over a period, as a level (annual labor market earnings / wage income).

nodes.label: Means-tested transfer program
nodes.summary: A public benefit paid only to those whose means are low enough.

nodes.label: Asset test
nodes.summary: The rule that takes a benefit away from people holding too much in liquid assets.

nodes.label: Income transparency norms
nodes.summary: Whether talking openly about one's income is normal where a person lives and works.

nodes.label: Income replacement rate
nodes.summary: The share of income lost to a shock that is made up by public transfers and other insurance.

nodes.label: Sickness benefit receipt
nodes.summary: The sick-pay transfers a person receives from the public purse while unable to work.

nodes.label: Socio-economic status
nodes.summary: How high a person stands in terms of income, schooling and occupation.

nodes.label: Taxable income reported to the tax authority
nodes.summary: The income a taxpayer reports on the tax return and is taxed on, summed over all sources.

nodes.label: Self-reported income
nodes.summary: The part of reported taxable income that the taxpayer declares himself, with no third party filing it to the tax authority.

nodes.label: Third-party reported income
nodes.summary: The part of reported taxable income that an employer, bank or other third party files directly to the tax authority and that arrives prepopulated on the return.

nodes.label: Type of job applied for
nodes.summary: Which sorts of jobs someone chooses to apply for.

nodes.label: Applications to part-time jobs
nodes.summary: How much of someone's job hunting is aimed at part-time work.

nodes.label: Applications to jobs with a short commute
nodes.summary: How much of someone's job hunting is aimed at jobs near home.

nodes.label: Reallocation of workers between firms
nodes.summary: How much the workforce shifts from one firm to another rather than moving around inside firms.

nodes.label: Appointment to a board directorship
nodes.summary: Getting appointed to a company board as a director.

nodes.label: Career success
nodes.summary: Career success is how far a worker advances in pay and seniority over his working life.

nodes.label: Cost of supplying labor
nodes.summary: How costly it is for someone to take on market work.

nodes.label: Co-workers' hours of work
nodes.summary: How long the people a person works with put in at work.

nodes.label: Embeddedness in the corporate elite
nodes.summary: This is how tied into the network of other top executives and directors a manager is.

nodes.label: Moves to higher-paying employers
nodes.summary: How much a worker works his way up to better-paying firms.

nodes.label: Acceptance of ex-offenders
nodes.summary: How willing employers and the public are to accept people who have been in prison.

nodes.label: Wage premium for ex-offenders
nodes.summary: How much more (or less) workers with a prison record are paid than similar workers without one.

nodes.label: Family friendliness of the employer
nodes.summary: How accommodating of workers with young children the firm a worker is employed at is.

nodes.label: Working at a firm with mothers in management
nodes.summary: Whether a worker is employed at a firm whose management includes women with young children.

nodes.label: Working in the public sector
nodes.summary: Whether a worker is employed by the public sector rather than a private firm.

nodes.label: Gender gap in jobs applied for
nodes.summary: How far apart women's and men's job applications are in the sorts of jobs they target.

nodes.label: Gender gap in career success
nodes.summary: The gender career gap is how much less far women get in pay and seniority than comparable men.

nodes.label: Gender gap in earnings from children
nodes.summary: The percentage by which women's earnings fall behind men's because of children -- the child penalty in earnings.

nodes.label: Gender gap in productivity
nodes.summary: How far men's measured productivity at work runs ahead of women's.

nodes.label: Gender gap in wages
nodes.summary: How much less women are paid than comparable men.

nodes.label: Horizontal wage dispersion within the firm
nodes.summary: How unequal pay is among colleagues doing comparable-level work.

nodes.label: Immigrant-native wage gap
nodes.summary: How much less immigrants are paid than comparable natives.

nodes.label: Job displacement
nodes.summary: Whether a worker loses his job because the employer cuts jobs or shuts down.

nodes.label: Job finding
nodes.summary: Job finding is how readily an unemployed person gets back into work.

nodes.label: Job polarization
nodes.summary: How hollowed-out the middle of the occupational wage distribution is: employment concentrated at the low and high ends relative to the middle.

nodes.label: Job search intensity
nodes.summary: Search intensity is how hard someone looking for work actually searches.

nodes.label: Prior labor market history
nodes.summary: A person's own record of work and earnings before the event under study.

nodes.label: Labor supply
nodes.summary: How much work a person supplies to the market, on the participation and hours margins taken together.

nodes.label: Hours of work
nodes.summary: Hours worked per period, conditional on working -- the intensive margin of labor supply.

nodes.label: Paid absence from work
nodes.summary: How many paid days a worker spends off the job rather than at work.

nodes.label: Labor force participation
nodes.summary: Whether a person works at all -- the extensive margin of labor supply.

nodes.label: Local labor market conditions
nodes.summary: Local labor market conditions are how plentiful jobs are where a person lives.

nodes.label: Switching between main and secondary employment
nodes.summary: How much a worker moves work and pay between his primary job and a side job.

nodes.label: Male share of the professional network
nodes.summary: How male-dominated a person's professional contacts are.

nodes.label: Female share of own occupation
nodes.summary: How female-dominated the job a person chooses to work in is.

nodes.label: Employment by occupational wage tier
nodes.summary: Whether a worker is employed in an occupation of a given position in the occupational wage distribution.

nodes.label: Employment in high-wage occupations
nodes.summary: Whether a worker holds a job in the top of the occupational wage distribution.

nodes.label: Employment in low-wage occupations
nodes.summary: Whether a worker holds a job in the bottom of the occupational wage distribution.

nodes.label: Employment in mid-wage occupations
nodes.summary: Whether a worker holds a job in the middle of the occupational wage distribution.

nodes.label: Occupational mobility
nodes.summary: A worker's movement between occupations of different wage tiers.

nodes.label: Downward occupational mobility
nodes.summary: Moving from a mid-wage occupation into a lower-wage one.

nodes.label: Upward occupational mobility
nodes.summary: Moving from a mid-wage occupation into a higher-wage one.

nodes.label: Occupational rank
nodes.summary: A worker's position in the occupational hierarchy.

nodes.label: Holding a managerial position
nodes.summary: Whether a worker holds a management job.

nodes.label: Paid parental leave entitlement
nodes.summary: Paid parental leave entitlement is how much paid time off from work parents may take around the birth of a child.

nodes.label: Earmarked (non-transferable) leave
nodes.summary: Earmarked leave is the share of paid parental leave reserved for one parent and lost if unused.

nodes.label: Marginal cost of a day of parental leave
nodes.summary: This is what a household loses in income for taking one more day of parental leave.

nodes.label: Cost of the parental leave system
nodes.summary: What the parental leave system costs the public purse.

nodes.label: Take-up of parental leave
nodes.summary: Take-up of parental leave is whether and how long eligible workers actually use the leave they are entitled to.

nodes.label: Decoupling of pay and productivity
nodes.summary: How far apart a worker's pay and his own productivity stand.

nodes.label: Propensity to leave the current employer
nodes.summary: How likely a worker is to walk away from his current job.

nodes.label: Routine-task intensity of the occupation
nodes.summary: How routine the tasks of a job are.

nodes.label: Statutory retirement age
nodes.summary: The official age at which people may retire on a public pension.

nodes.label: Time spent in retirement
nodes.summary: How long someone's retirement lasts.

nodes.label: Unemployment
nodes.summary: This is how much time a person spends jobless and looking for work.

nodes.label: Wage rate
nodes.summary: Pay per hour of work -- earnings divided by hours.

nodes.label: Earnings rank within the firm
nodes.summary: How high up a worker sits on his own firm's pay ladder.

nodes.label: Accumulated work experience
nodes.summary: How much working time a person has accumulated over his career so far.

nodes.label: Real interest rate
nodes.summary: The return to saving once inflation is netted out, which sets the price of spending now rather than later.

nodes.label: Recession
nodes.summary: A period when the economy as a whole is shrinking.

nodes.label: Emigration
nodes.summary: Emigration is moving out of the country to live abroad.

nodes.label: Immigrant status
nodes.summary: Whether someone is an immigrant rather than native-born.

nodes.label: Openness of immigration policy
nodes.summary: Openness of immigration policy is how far the rules let foreigners come in and work.

nodes.label: Restrictions on family reunification
nodes.summary: Family-reunification restrictions are the conditions a resident must meet to bring a foreign spouse or relative into the country.

nodes.label: Linguistic and cultural barriers
nodes.summary: How far language and cultural differences keep a migrant from using the services and institutions around him.

nodes.label: Local immigrant share of the workforce
nodes.summary: This is how much of a municipality's workforce is immigrant rather than native-born.

nodes.label: Country of origin
nodes.summary: Country of origin is which country a migrant or a migrant parent came from.

nodes.label: Years since migration
nodes.summary: How many years an immigrant has been in the country.

nodes.label: External funding
nodes.summary: How much funding an organization raises from outside sources.

nodes.label: Government project funds
nodes.summary: Public money given for a particular project rather than for running the organization.

nodes.label: Targeted private project funds
nodes.summary: Private foundation money given for a particular project rather than for running the organization.

nodes.label: General public operating grants
nodes.summary: Public core funding an organization may spend on running itself.

nodes.label: Outsourcing of service provision
nodes.summary: Having an outside private provider deliver a service instead of doing it in-house.

nodes.label: Community background
nodes.summary: Everything children share by being raised in the same place, treated as a single influence on how their lives turn out.

nodes.label: Education level of the neighbourhood
nodes.summary: This is how much schooling the adults in a child's neighbourhood have.

nodes.label: Income level of the neighbourhood
nodes.summary: This is how high the incomes of the households in a child's neighbourhood are.

nodes.label: Physical proximity to others
nodes.summary: How near a person is, in daily life, to the people in his comparison group.

nodes.label: Region of upbringing
nodes.summary: The part of the country a person grew up in.

nodes.label: Economic preferences
nodes.summary: A person's underlying tastes over risk and the timing of money, which shape his financial choices.

nodes.label: Household utility
nodes.summary: How well off a household is by its own reckoning.

nodes.label: Patience
nodes.summary: Patience is how willing a person is to wait for a later, larger reward.

nodes.label: Reference dependence
nodes.summary: How much a person judges an outcome by how it compares with a reference point rather than by what it is worth.

nodes.label: Risk tolerance
nodes.summary: How willing a person is to take on financial risk.

nodes.label: Subjective well-being
nodes.summary: How satisfied people say they are with their life and its various parts.

nodes.label: Social isolation
nodes.summary: Being cut off from other people, with few contacts outside the home.

nodes.label: Behavioral response to taxation
nodes.summary: How strongly people change their behaviour and their reported income when taxes change.

nodes.label: Employer willingness to cooperate in shifting
nodes.summary: How willing the firm a worker is employed at is to retime wage payments so the worker can shift income between tax years.

nodes.label: Government revenue
nodes.summary: Government revenue is the money the state takes in, net of what it pays out in benefits.

nodes.label: Intertemporal income shifting
nodes.summary: Moving income between tax periods to have it taxed at the lower rate.

nodes.label: Legal tax avoidance
nodes.summary: Lawful rearrangement of income or deductions to reduce tax owed.

nodes.label: Marginal tax rate
nodes.summary: The share of the next krone of income taken in tax.

nodes.label: Marginal tax rate on capital income
nodes.summary: The marginal tax rate applying to income from assets.

nodes.label: Marginal tax rate on labor income
nodes.summary: The marginal tax rate applying to income from work.

nodes.label: Tax enforcement exposure
nodes.summary: How much verification a taxpayer's income is subject to, whether by audit, by announced audit risk, or by third-party information reporting.

nodes.label: Tax audit
nodes.summary: Having one's tax return actually audited.

nodes.label: Threat-of-audit letter
nodes.summary: Receiving a letter announcing that one's return faces a stated probability of audit.

nodes.label: Third-party information reporting
nodes.summary: Whether an income item is filed to the tax authority by an employer, bank or other third party rather than left to the taxpayer.

nodes.label: Tax evasion
nodes.summary: Income illegally hidden from the tax authority, as an amount or as a share of true income.

nodes.label: Tax salience
nodes.summary: How aware of and attentive to the tax change a taxpayer is.

nodes.label: Business hours overlap with foreign partners
nodes.summary: How much a firm's working day overlaps with that of the foreign firms it trades with.

nodes.label: Import competition
nodes.summary: How much competition from imports a worker's industry or occupation faces.

nodes.label: Bequest received
nodes.summary: Wealth transferred to a person at the death of a parent.

nodes.label: Holding wealth as cash
nodes.summary: How much money someone keeps as cash instead of in the bank.

nodes.label: Debt
nodes.summary: How much a person owes in total.

nodes.label: Default on debt
nodes.summary: Whether a person falls into arrears or defaults on his debt.

nodes.label: Financial behaviour
nodes.summary: A person's persistent way of handling money, borrowing and repayment, of the kind children pick up from their parents.

nodes.label: Accessing home equity
nodes.summary: Turning the value of one's home into money that can be spent.

nodes.label: Policy access to home equity
nodes.summary: How far the rules make it possible to borrow against one's home.

nodes.label: Liquidity constraint
nodes.summary: How tightly a person's lack of liquid assets relative to income limits what she can do with the timing of her money.

nodes.label: Mandated funded pension plans
nodes.summary: Rules obliging workers to save into funded pension accounts.

nodes.label: Net wealth
nodes.summary: The stock of wealth a person holds -- assets net of debt.

nodes.label: Inclusion of pension wealth in measured wealth
nodes.summary: This is how far pension entitlements are counted as part of someone's wealth.

nodes.label: Saving
nodes.summary: Saving is the part of income a person puts aside instead of spending.

nodes.label: Contributions to employer-sponsored retirement accounts
nodes.summary: What goes into a person's workplace pension account.

nodes.label: Contributions to personal retirement accounts
nodes.summary: What a person puts aside in a private pension account of his own.

nodes.label: Wealth inequality
nodes.summary: How unequally wealth is spread across people.

nodes.label: Absolute wealth inequality
nodes.summary: Dispersion of wealth measured in kroner -- how far apart people's wealth levels are.

nodes.label: Relative wealth inequality
nodes.summary: Dispersion of wealth measured in shares -- how much of total wealth the top holds.
